standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-compactness of the preimage of a quasi-compact open under a quasi-compact morphism
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes $f^{-1}(V)$ quasi-compact for a quasi-compact open $V \subset Y$, which is what allows the local finiteness of the family $\{Z_i\}$ to be used.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local finiteness of a family of closed subsets on a quasi-compact space
standard_prerequisites.use: On the quasi-compact open $f^{-1}(V)$ only finitely many of the closed sets $Z_i$ meet it, which is the finiteness claimed for the image family.

core_obligations: Fix a quasi-compact open subset $V \subset Y$ (proof line 1858).

Use quasi-compactness of $f$ to make $f^{-1}(V)$ quasi-compact, and the local finiteness of $\{Z_i\}$ to conclude that only finitely many $i$ have $Z_i \cap f^{-1}(V) \neq \emptyset$ (proof lines 1859-1862).
Identify that index set with the set of $i$ with $\overline{f(Z_i)} \cap V \neq \emptyset$, which proves the local finiteness of the image family (proof lines 1863-1867).
proof_roadmap: Choice of a quasi-compact open in the target (proof line 1858).
Finiteness of the indices meeting the preimage (proof lines 1859-1862).
Identification of the index sets (proof lines 1863-1867).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that pushing forward a locally finite family of closed subsets along a quasi-compact morphism keeps the family of closures locally finite (statement lines 1846-1855). The proof tests local finiteness against an arbitrary quasi-compact open of the target, uses quasi-compactness of the morphism to pull it back to a quasi-compact open where the family is finite, and identifies the relevant index sets. The reduction to quasi-compact opens is the substance, so the claim is H2.
